species.real: In the 1800s Swansea was nicknamed Copperopolis, and the smelting smoke was so poisonous that the hills of the lower Swansea valley were left almost bare.
species.name: Smeltling

dex.text: A lump of glowing slag that crawls off the old copper tips at night and sits by any warm chimney it can find. Leaves green footprints on everything.
dex.fact: Smelting copper took more coal than ore, so ore was shipped from Cornwall, and later from Chile and Cuba, to Swansea's coalfield. By the 1800s the town was nicknamed Copperopolis.

species.real: Copper kills many bacteria that land on it within hours, which is why old brass door handles and rails are cleaner than they look.
species.name: Cuprion

dex.text: Polished copper where it's proud of itself and green verdigris where it isn't. Sparks run along its plates in a thunderstorm, and it hums when you stand too close.
dex.fact: Copper carries electricity better than any metal except silver, which is why it is in nearly every wire in your house. Swansea copper also sheathed the hulls of the Navy's wooden warships.
